look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST — HENBIT: a cool-season ANNUAL mint with squarish/4-angled stems and OPPOSITE leaf pairs. The LOWER leaves have stalks (petioles). HIGHER flowering leaves are ROUND/KIDNEY- to FAN-SHAPED, COARSELY SCALLOPED and SESSILE, forming a CLASPING COLLAR around the stem. PINK-PURPLE LONG TUBES with a HOODED UPPER LIP rise in clustered WHORLS at upper leaf nodes. This leaf stalk transition is the best split from L. purpureum (purple deadnettle), whose upper leaves remain stalked and tend to be more triangular/pointed and often purplish. Glechoma hederacea (ground ivy) is a perennial creeping stolon-former with stalked round leaves; it is NOT henbit.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Winter annual in Central Texas, typically low/sprawling and 10–40 cm tall; bases can branch or root where stems touch moist soil. Flowers mainly in cooler weather and spring. Not a perennial spreader.

key_traits.label: Root
key_traits.text: Shallow branching/fibrous or short-taproot system; roots and node-rooting not visible in current two installed photos.

key_traits.label: Stem
key_traits.text: Square/four-angled stem, often green to reddish purple, sparingly hairy; inspect the CROSS SECTION with fingertips or angled macro, not proven by a frontal photo.

key_traits.label: Leaves arrangement
key_traits.text: Opposite at each node; lower pairs with petioles and upper pairs sessile/clasping. IMPORTANT: upper whorls can look like one continuous green collar when seen from above.

key_traits.label: Upper leaf
key_traits.text: Upper leafy bracts 5–18 mm, round to kidney/fan-shaped, crenate/coarsely lobed, lack a distinct petiole and partly surround the flowering stem (amplexicaul = stem embracing).

key_traits.label: Lower leaf
key_traits.text: Lower leaves rounded/heart-shaped with a PETIOLE (small leaf stalk). Scalloped blunt lobes, prominent palmately spreading veins.

key_traits.label: Flowers
key_traits.text: Axillary verticillasters (false whorls) among opposite upper leaves; pink-to-purple bilabiate corolla about 10–20 mm, noticeably elongated slender tube and hairy arched upper lip; lower lip with spots and lobes.

key_traits.label: Calyx
key_traits.text: Five-toothed tubular green calyx persists after the corolla falls. Individual calyx teeth are not scored in currently installed pictures.

key_traits.label: Fruits
key_traits.text: Schizocarp splitting into FOUR small nutlets, initially enclosed by the persistent calyx. Need genuine mature nutlet/dissected calyx macro with mm rule.

key_traits.label: Seasonal
key_traits.text: In Hays County, often germinates in fall and flowers in winter/spring when moisture is available; can appear elsewhere in cooler damp seasons. Timing is supportive, not species-proof.
